core.title: Declare acceptance boundary kinds only from the controlled vocabulary
core.given: An acceptance declares the named integration surfaces (boundary kind values) it exercises
core.when: You write, edit or review its boundary kind entries
core.then: Use only values from the controlled boundary kind vocabulary: argv, subprocess, filesystem, git, http_wire, llm_wire, cmux_rpc, env_config, db_wire, event_wire.
prefer: Pick the value whose definition matches the surface exercised: argv = command-line argument vector passed to a process; subprocess = a child process spawned and observed; filesystem = files and directories read or written; git = a local git repository's objects, refs and config; http_wire = HTTP request/response envelopes (cassette when hermetic); llm_wire = LLM prompt/response envelopes (recorded/deterministic when hermetic); cmux_rpc = cmux RPC request/response messages; env_config = environment variables and configuration inputs; db_wire = database query/response envelopes; event_wire = event-bus publish/consume envelopes.
avoid: Inventing, abbreviating or synonym-ing boundary kind values outside the vocabulary — unknown values are rejected by the acceptance contract validator.
Listing `golden` as a boundary kind: `golden` is a harness code, not a boundary kind — a harness code classifies how a surface is exercised hermetically, not which surface is exercised.
core.why: The boundary kind is a controlled vocabulary of named integration surfaces an acceptance exercises; unknown values are rejected.
evidence: The acceptance contract validator reports no unknown boundary kind values for the acceptance.
Every boundary kind in the acceptance is one of the ten vocabulary values and none is `golden`.
verification: A validation check rejects any boundary kind value that is not in the controlled vocabulary; the finding applies to every acceptance, including unchanged declarations that already contain unknown values.

The check covers only boundary kind declarations in acceptances: it does not cover harness code entries (governed by the sibling harness-code vocabulary) or production code changes that add an integration surface.

values: boundary kind value added or edited in an acceptance
unknown boundary kind value reported by the boundary kind validator

fires: A planner writes an acceptance that declares boundary kind values.
A planner edits an existing acceptance's boundary declaration (adds, renames or removes a boundary kind).
A planner reviews or validates existing acceptances and finds a boundary kind value (unchanged or not) outside the vocabulary, e.g. `golden`.
A planner is deciding whether a golden-file comparison belongs in the acceptance's boundary kind list.
doesNotFire: Acceptance edits that neither add, change nor review boundary kind declarations.
Editing only harness code values with no boundary kind involved (governed by the harness-code vocabulary, not this rule).
Production code changes that introduce a new integration surface without any acceptance boundary declaration being written or reviewed.

profileRequirements.meaning: How the stack identifies acceptance spec files — the concrete artifact kind that plays the acceptance_test role. The activation fact file_kind takes its value from this key, so the rule knows which files carry boundary kind declarations.

neutralityNotes: The whole convention is a controlled-vocabulary rule over the ATDD acceptance declaration, which is methodology-level rather than stack-level: the ten boundary kinds (argv, subprocess, filesystem, git, http_wire, llm_wire, cmux_rpc, env_config, db_wire, event_wire) and their definitions are kept verbatim in the core, because they name integration-surface categories, not stacks, runtimes, frameworks, languages, package managers, suffixes or paths. cmux_rpc names this product's own RPC surface (a domain datum, not a code-stack dependency), and cassette/recorded-when-hermetic are generic hermetic-testing mechanisms; if a future stack's methodology were to define a different set of integration surfaces, the vocabulary would have to become a profile datum (no existing vocabulary key covers it — idiom keys describe code constructs, not acceptance-declaration vocabularies). The declaration spellings boundary_kind/exercised_boundaries/harness_code/golden are treated as shared ATDD methodology terms and kept. The only genuinely Bun-specific content is the validator/finding id tester.acceptance-violation.hermetic-fake-must-declare-contract and the Decision #7 audit pointer, both bunOnly; the core's verification describes the same check generically with the same scope (all acceptances, including unchanged declarations) and the same non-coverage (harness codes, production code).
